# netbox_platform (Resource)

From the [official documentation](https://docs.netbox.dev/en/stable/features/devices/#platforms):

> A platform defines the type of software running on a device or virtual machine. This can be helpful to model when it is necessary to distinguish between different versions or feature sets. Note that two devices of the same type may be assigned different platforms: For example, one Juniper MX240 might run Junos 14 while another runs Junos 15.

## Example Usage

```terraform
// Resource for PanOS (e.g. Panorama from Palo Alto)
resource "netbox_platform" "PANOS" {
  name = "PANOS"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the platform.

### Optional

- `comments` (String) Free-form comments about the platform.
- `config_template_id` (Number) The ID of the config template associated with the platform.
- `custom_fields` (Map of String) Custom field values of the object, as a map of field name to value.
- `description` (String) A description of the platform.
- `manufacturer_id` (Number) The ID of the manufacturer associated with the platform.
- `owner_id` (Number) The ID of the owner associated with the platform. Needs NetBox 4.5.0 or later.
- `parent_id` (Number) The ID of the parent associated with the platform.
- `slug` (String) The URL-friendly slug of the platform.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags assigned to the object, by name.

### Read-Only

- `created` (String) When the platform was created.
- `device_count` (Number) The number of device objects that refer to the platform.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `last_updated` (String) When the platform was last changed.
- `tags_all` (Set of String) All tags assigned to the object, including those not managed by Terraform.
- `virtualmachine_count` (Number) The number of virtualmachine objects that refer to the platform.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The ID is the numeric NetBox ID of the object
terraform import netbox_platform.example 1
```
